parties: K.P. Energy Limited; Raz Holding Group
headline: K.P. Energy and Raz Holding Group sign Non-Binding Letter of Intent for Strategic Investment and/or Collaboration
sum: K.P. Energy Limited and Raz Holding Group have executed a non-binding Letter of Intent for a proposed strategic investment and/or collaboration. The LOI, disclosed via NSE filing on 24 August 2026, contemplates potential capital infusion and/or operational partnership in the renewable energy sector.
implication: Non-binding LOI signals early-stage strategic exploration; partners should monitor for subsequent binding agreements, regulatory clearances (FDI if foreign capital involved, CCI if >₹2,000 cr and acquisition threshold breached) and material announcements under Listing Rules.
detail: K.P. Energy Limited, a listed renewable energy company, has signed a non-binding Letter of Intent with Raz Holding Group for a strategic investment and/or collaboration. The transaction structure-whether equity investment, debt, or operational partnership-remains unspecified in the public disclosure. The LOI is non-binding and contemplates further due diligence and negotiation of binding transaction documents. Standard regulatory approvals (CCI merger clearance if applicable, RBI ECB/FDI norms if foreign capital, NCLT if any scheme) will likely follow upon execution of definitive agreements.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 30
framework.note: central - mandatory disclosure of material events and updates (LOI, strategic partnerships) to stock exchanges.
central - CCI merger/combination notification required if deal crosses ₹2,000 cr asset threshold or 25% control acquisition.
central - if Raz Holding is a foreign entity, FDI route (Liberalised Remittance Scheme or Equity Entry Route) and RBI approval/notification may apply.
amended - if investment/guarantee exceeds prescribed thresholds, board and shareholder approvals; 'related party' rules if Raz is related.
- environmental clearance if renewable energy project expansion triggers Schedule 1 thresholds.
- relevant if any scheme of arrangement or restructuring contemplated post-investment.

framework.ref: Ministry of Power, Government of India – Renewable Energy Policy Guidelines
framework.note: - sector-specific allocation, grid evacuation, and incentive rules applicable to renewable projects.

conditions: Non-binding LOI; contemplates further due diligence
Binding definitive agreements to be negotiated
RBI FDI/ECB approval (if Raz is foreign entity)
K.P. Energy board and shareholder approvals for material investment
Regulatory approvals from Ministry of Power / electricity regulator (if grid-connected renewable asset)
approvals: K.P. Energy Board approval (likely before LOI signature)
CCI merger notification (if deal value/asset threshold crossed)
Ministry of Power / MNRE clearance (sector-specific, if applicable)
structure.novel: Non-binding LOI stage with strategic optionality (investment and/or collaboration) suggests open-architecture negotiation; absence of consideration figure and deal structure in public disclosure indicates early-stage exploration.

triggers.note: Combination notification threshold if Raz Holding acquires >₹2,000 cr assets or >25% control in K.P. Energy.
FDI route clearance if Raz Holding is a non-resident entity or foreign company.
Continuous disclosure obligation on K.P. Energy; material updates (binding agreement, approval milestones) must be flagged to exchanges.
If investment amount exceeds ₹1 cr (or 5% of net worth), related-party transaction approval required from audit committee and shareholders.
